newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Waigel said to want political steer on EMU pact.
newsitem.headline: Waigel said to want political steer on EMU pact.

text.p: European Union diplomats said on Tuesday German Finance Minister Theo Waigel wanted political direction from the top before agreeing a budget disciplinary pact among those joining monetary union.
At a meeting of EU finance ministers on Monday, Waigel was apparently confronted by colleagues who told him that agreement was possible that evening.
Waigel was said to have replied that it would be better to wait for political direction from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac who meet next Monday.

Following the Kohl-Chirac meeting, the EU's monetary committee could easily gather on Tuesday to hammer out a final compromise, which would then be considered by finance ministers on Thursday, Waigel said.

EU finance ministers remained deadlocked on Monday over a definition of "exceptional and temporary circumstances" which would let a country with an excessive deficit avoid fines. -- Brussels newsroom 32 2 287 6830
